title: Development of a polysiloxane network with hybrid pendants featuring an improved  N -halamine to quaternary ammonium salt proportion for superior biocidability
content: Increasing the N-halamine to quaternary ammonium salt (QAS) ratio within the hybrid pendants of a polysiloxane network has been verified as an effective approach for enhancing biocidability on cellulose. Specifically, the QAS precursor, 2-(dimethylamino)ethan-1-ol, and the imide and amide N-halamine precursors, 5-(4-hydroxybutyl)imidazolidine-2,4-dione, were sequentially attached to 3-allyldihydrofuran-2,5-dione through alcoholysis reactions. The dimethylamino group and C═  C of the resultant compound were reacted with 1-chloroheptane and trimethoxysilane via quaternization and hydrosilylation, respectively, to produce a saline that was hydrolyzed and condensed into a crosslinked polysiloxane layer with side groups consisting of one QAS and two N–H bonds on cellulose. After chlorination of the N–H bonds, the cellulose was encapsulated with an 89.6 nm thick layer containing the target hybrid pendants of one QAS and two N-halamine sites. Antibacterial kinetic studies demonstrated enhanced biocidability, as the higher proportion of N-halamine achieved eradications of E. coli and S. aureus at ∼107 CFU within 5 min, outperforming a reported counterpart containing one QAS and one N-halamine. The stability and rechargeability tests indicated that the cyclic N-halamines and crosslinked polysiloxane contribute to a robust biocidability. This study presents an approach for higher biocidability by combining a larger number of N-halamines with one cationic component.
